Copied file line 31 is exactly the comment '-- The solution was adapted from here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PNFh789P31E.' (line 32 is the indexing note). Quote is verbatim.

Decomposition matches the code and closes: parent egmo2023_p1 fixes min m / max M (lines 33-34), children h1 (lines 35-44) and h2 (lines 45-54) are two-link calc chains bounding b m >= 2 and b M <= 2, and the proof closes via h3 (eq_of_le_of_ge, lines 55-59) then the goal (lines 60-63); provenance passes (byte-identical at 1745e6c) and CI push-main.yaml runs lake build. However the children's closed_by fields misdescribe the gcongr subgoals. In h1 the first gcongr goal is the denominator-positivity 0 <= a m, closed by le_of_lt (ha m) (from ha, not hm) - the entry writes 'a m <= a m ... from hm'. In h2 the corresponding 0 <= a M goal (le_of_lt (ha M)) is omitted entirely. Fix: correct the parentheticals to '0 <= a m (le_of_lt (ha m)), a m <= a (m-1), a m <= a (m+1) from hm' and '0 <= a M (le_of_lt (ha M)), a (M-1) <= a M, a (M+1) <= a M from hM'.

Generality holds. The move is stated beyond the example: applicability.goal_shape abstracts the domain to 'an inequality E >= c or E <= c over an ordered ring', the expression to 'a ratio or sum', and the closing tactics to 'rewriting plus positivity/norm_num' (entry.json:90-91), and use_when factors the pattern into a monotonicity link (gcongr) + an algebra link (rw/positivity) + an antisymmetry close (entry.json:92) — a reusable 'bound a derived quantity at min/max, then eq_of_le_of_ge' template, not EGMO-specific. Consequences are honest and specific: one obligation per link; transitivity discharged by calc itself; the monotonicity link needs gcongr to find hm/hM facts and the algebra link needs a i > 0 for positivity [ha i]; the close needs BOTH directions because eq_of_le_of_ge won't fire with one side (entry.json:128; README:152-160). When-not-to-use is largely specific (non-monotone link; link needing its own lemma; long chains of real lemmas). Minor imprecision only: the clause 'the bounds are strict (<) and the exactness of the constant matters' (entry.json:93) is loosely worded — it does not harm the move's general statement (the antisymmetry close genuinely requires non-strict >= / <= bounds), but could be sharpened to say 'the close needs non-strict bounds; strict-only bounds cannot feed eq_of_le_of_ge'. Not a standing objection.
